finding.claim: inverseForFile (and inverseForDirectory at line 58) maps any Unix mode other than exactly 0644/0600 (or 0755/0700) to PUBLIC, so a restricted source file (e.g. mode 0640, 0660, 0400) is treated as public; a cross-mount copy with retain_visibility then writes it world-readable at the destination.
finding.source: File mode of a file on a source mount (precondition: non-standard restrictive mode such as 0640/0660/0400). Adapter code that calls inverseForFile is not in this repository and was not verified.
finding.sink: Destination write with visibility=public, which PortableVisibilityConverter::forFile maps to filePublic (0644).

trace.note: fallback returns Visibility::PUBLIC for any unrecognized mode
if no explicit visibility and retain enabled, visibility is read from source
sourceFilesystem->visibility(sourcePath) returns the reported (possibly widened) value
forFile maps PUBLIC to filePublic (0644) at destination

finding.guards_checked: PortableVisibilityGuard::guardAgainstInvalidInput (PortableVisibilityGuard.php:11) validates only the requested visibility string, not the source mode. retain_visibility default true (MountManager.php:394; Filesystem.php:284). No check that the source mode is actually world-readable before widening.

finding.claim: publicUrl() concatenates the normalized path into the URL without percent-encoding, so ?, # or % characters in a filename are interpreted as query/fragment syntax (ShardedPrefixPublicUrlGenerator.php:37 has the same issue).
finding.source: Filename or path containing ?, #, or % chosen by an uploader and passed to publicUrl().
finding.sink: Returned public URL string, typically embedded in HTML, email, or redirects by the application.

trace.note: path normalized, which strips . and .. and control characters but not ?#%
prefixPath only ltrims leading slashes; no encoding

finding.guards_checked: WhitespacePathNormalizer blocks .. above root and control characters, so path traversal out of the URL prefix is blocked. No URL encoding of ?, #, % anywhere on the path. Impact depends on application use of publicUrl with user-chosen names.

finding.claim: Filesystem-level retain_visibility takes precedence over a per-call retain_visibility option, unlike MountManager (line 394) where per-call wins; a caller passing retain_visibility=false is ignored when the filesystem default is true, so the source's visibility is kept on copy/move.
finding.source: Per-call $config['retain_visibility'] = false passed to Filesystem::copy() or Filesystem::move().
finding.sink: Destination visibility of the copied/moved file.

trace.note: $this->config->get(RETAIN, per-call value) returns filesystem default true if set, ignoring per-call false
retainVisibility true and no explicit per-call visibility
default visibility removed, so source visibility is used

finding.guards_checked: Explicit per-call visibility is honored (Filesystem.php:292). MountManager.php:394 uses per-call precedence, so behavior is inconsistent across the two layers. Impact requires a filesystem configured with retain_visibility=true and a public source.
